method_notes: Method B: decomposed node hit area, retained dragging and selection-enabled deletion, and the pointer-location to hit-target to selection relationship before querying.
Query 1 sought same-domain candidates; query 2 expressed the overlap/interactive-child relation without naming a donor field or target product.
Only system2_search_query was used, in English. No shell networking, original-issue retrieval, GitHub API, same-issue PR, release, or resolution inspection.
Search-result titles, URLs, references, and order are recorded exactly as displayed. seen_content values are short paraphrases of exposure, not claims of direct reading.
Initial page segments and ineffective anchor navigation are distinguished from direct section reads. All click/find/reopen actions count against the six-open budget.
All three forms remain within the web UI domain; no cross-domain novelty is asserted.
The provided input hash is preserved as assignment metadata and was not independently recomputed.
UTC invocation and return times were measured with the orchestration runtime clock for every web action. The preliminary local prompt read occurred before timed research and was not separately timed.
Candidate summaries are under 160 words each; no direct prose quotes are reproduced. Proposed tests are original synthesis, not executed results.
Unmentioned alternatives are only absent from the supplied post; no claim is made about what its author knew.

final_candidates.title: CSS Basic User Interface Module Level 4
final_candidates.exact_section: 6.2 Exclusion from Hit-testing: the pointer-events property; returned lines 825–849
final_candidates.verification_status: Directly read through counted find action; earlier opens exposed only the opening segment.
final_candidates.page_summary: The standard separates pointer hit testing from event propagation. An excluded parent can contain an explicitly targetable child; events from that child may still reach ancestor handlers. Keyboard focus is not disabled. Normal hit testing still has unspecified corners.
final_candidates.input_processing_observation: Pointer outside an enabled descendant bypasses an excluded front box; a pointer inside the descendant targets it and can propagate to ancestors.
final_candidates.what_is_new_vs_baseline: The baseline disables node selectability. This suggests restricting the browser hit area while retaining node selectability; it is absent from the supplied post, not proved unknown to its author.
final_candidates.changed_choice: Propose excluding the actual outer node box and re-enabling a small child hit area. Check that React Flow honors that styling before adopting it.
final_candidates.minimal_discriminating_input: PROPOSED T1: two overlapping selectable nodes A behind B; B has one enabled child H and a drag handle. Compare a click outside H, a click on H, deletion after selecting B, and a drag from its handle.
final_candidates.expected_output: Proposed acceptance: outside H selects A; H selects B; the configured delete action removes B; dragging its handle moves B. CSS supports target routing, but all React Flow outcomes remain unexecuted.
limitations: React Flow wrapper styling and handlers are unverified.
CSS hit testing does not itself set application selection or perform deletion.
Actual library version and browser behavior are unknown.
final_candidates.counter_evidence: The standard explicitly leaves hit-testing corners unresolved. Styling only an inner node body can leave an outer wrapper targetable; this is a proposed failure case.
final_candidates.historical_availability: Unknown for 2024-01-01. The directly read edition is dated 2026; earlier editions were linked but not opened.

final_candidates.title: Utility Classes - React Flow
final_candidates.version_or_date: Current documentation read 2026-11-24; publication date and package version unknown
final_candidates.page_summary: The nodrag class suppresses drag initiation and default node selection on its element. The nopan class controls viewport panning.
final_candidates.input_processing_observation: Interaction with a nodrag element suppresses specified React Flow behaviors; the page does not promise routing that pointer input to an overlapping node.
final_candidates.what_is_new_vs_baseline: Adds a negative control: suppression of front-node selection does not by itself establish click-through. The existing selectable:false workaround remains the author's baseline.
final_candidates.changed_choice: Use nodrag only when suppressing selection/drag is intended. Do not infer a selection handle or click-through mechanism from that class.
final_candidates.minimal_discriminating_input: PROPOSED T2: put a nodrag child in front node B over node A. Click it while recording the pointer target and selected node IDs; compare with T1's hit-test exclusion.
final_candidates.expected_output: Documented expectation: no default B selection or drag from that child. A receiving the event is unknown from this page and must be observed; suppression alone fails the requested click-through condition.
conditions_supported: Separately checks default node selection and dragging
Provides a failure control for overlap behavior
limitations: No claim that nodrag retargets pointer events.
No demonstrated deletion or child-only selection recipe.
final_candidates.counter_evidence: Putting nodrag on the intended drag area conflicts with preserving dragging from that area.
final_candidates.historical_availability: Unknown for 2024-01-01; no historical package or documentation edition was read.

final_candidates.title: The ReactFlow component - React Flow
final_candidates.version_or_date: Current documentation read 2026-11-24; publication date and package version unknown
final_candidates.exact_section: Common props: nodeDragThreshold; Interaction props: selectNodesOnDrag and elevateNodesOnSelect; Keyboard props: deleteKeyCode; returned lines 565, 688–689, 701–708
final_candidates.page_summary: Drag-induced selection is independently configurable and enabled by default. Selection can raise node stacking order. Keyboard deletion acts on selected elements.
final_candidates.input_processing_observation: A drag can change both position and selected state; subsequent selection can change which overlapping node is visually in front.
final_candidates.what_is_new_vs_baseline: Adds two discriminators absent from the post: selection caused by dragging and overlap order changed by selection. The baseline drag handle itself is not new.
final_candidates.changed_choice: Decide explicitly whether dragging should also select. Test click-through again after a selection instead of checking only the initial overlap.
final_candidates.minimal_discriminating_input: PROPOSED T3: reset overlapping A/B, drag B from its handle beyond the configured threshold with selectNodesOnDrag true and false, record position and selected IDs, then repeat the overlap click and delete action.
final_candidates.expected_output: Proposed acceptance: dragging remains possible in both configurations; default drag selection occurs in the true case. Confirm the false case has no other selection cause. Deletion targets the selected node; recheck overlap after elevation.
conditions_supported: Overlapping nodes before and after selection
limitations: Does not define a region-specific selection handle.
False-case interaction with application handlers needs execution.
No exact installed version was supplied.
final_candidates.counter_evidence: A click-only test can miss selection on drag; a one-shot overlap test can miss later stacking changes.
final_candidates.historical_availability: Unknown for 2024-01-01; the current docs cannot establish the original implementation.
